elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: New (k): "Garman shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence".

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: New (k): "... and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate".

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: New (k): "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000".

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: New (k): "where Garman processes any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Sparkling, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000" — the trigger covers every category of Customer data, not selected named types.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: New (k): "and workers' compensation insurance as required by law".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: New (k) final sentence: "Garman shall provide certificates of insurance to Sparkling on request."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O of not less than USD 2,000,000 exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cyber and privacy of not less than USD 5,000,000 exceeds the USD 2,000,000 fallback floor.

reasons: All six preferred elements are rendered in operative language as new subsection (k); the preferred level is complete and the fallback floors are exceeded as a consequence.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a concise new clause for a genuinely missing provision, and the drafter omitted the model-language extras ("at its own expense" and the one-year survival tail) that would otherwise have failed minimality. No existing words were deleted or paraphrased — retained paragraphs (b), (i) and (j) are unchanged.

The cyber trigger is drafted as "any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Sparkling," which satisfies the requirement that the Customer Data trigger cover every category rather than selected named data types.

Intent is preserved: the new subsection is additive within the General Matters series, creates no undefined terms or dangling cross-references, and does not contradict any retained allocation, remedy or commercial mechanic.
Note only (not a defect): the clause does not state "at its own expense" or a post-term maintenance period; neither is a checklist element, so their absence is correct for minimality.
